To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
T_H1 type immune response of the gut mucosal immune system plays a role in the protection of the gastrointestinal tract against the damage induced by stress.
the T_H1 type of cytokine secreted and cytotoxicity activity of iIEL and the subset ( Thy1 -) are enhanced in the early stage of experimental digestive ulcer induced by restraint stress.

the increased expression of IFN-gamma and IL-2 mRNA and the enhanced cytotoxicity in intraepithelial lymphocytes (IEL) from mice with digestive ulcer induced with water-immersion restraint may play an important role in the protection of the function of gastrointestinal mucosal barrier, while the subset (Th1) of IEL may not be the main source of IFN-g and IL-2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of stress-induced digestive ulcer.
the role of T_H1 in the pathogenesis of digestive ulcer.
the mechanism of the immune regulation of iIELs in digestive ulcer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in the level of T H1 type cytokines in the intestinal immune cells is one of the important mechanisms of the protection of gastrointestinal tract from stress induced digestive ulcer.

iIELs and Thy1 - subset are not responsible for the increase of T_H1 secretion and cytotoxicity, but other cells in the mucosa and submucosa of the gastrointestinal tract may be involved in the process.
T_H1 type of cytokine secretion and cytotoxicity are enhanced in iIEL from mice with digestive ulcer induced stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
iIEL is an important immune organ, and its subset (CD3+CD4+CD8-) is not responsible for the changes of T_H1 secretion and cytotoxicity.
the increased secretion of IFNγ and IL2 in iIELs may protect the function and structure of digestive tract.
T_H1 cytokine secretion by iIELs is a protective mechanism for the digestive tract.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the iIELs play an important role in maintaining homeostasis of gastrointestinal tract.
we have found that iIELs and their subsets play an important role in protecting the gastrointestinal tract.
iIEL is an important part of the mucosal immune system.
